R1.strength: Clear, correct verdict (INP fails, LCP/CLS pass), says plainly that lab TBT misses INP, and starts with measuring the real slow interaction instead of guessing.
R1.mistake: Never mentions the Modernizr 134 ms forced reflow or the viewport flag, owners are generic ('your developer'), and most fixes have no completion check.

penalties.why: 'a subset with only the 20 to 30 icons the site actually uses' is an invented number not in the report

R2.strength: Strong WordPress-specific INP fix list (header.php viewport, Font Awesome JS swap, Modernizr removal, AddThis removal, defer, Joyride on click, Disqus dequeue) with a TTFB fix ranked second.
R2.mistake: Invents specifics (20 to 30 icons; implies Bootstrap tooltips sit on all 34 flagged links) and leans on jargon (MutationObserver, APO, immutable) a non-developer would not follow.

penalties.why: States 'SEO and accessibility should go to 90s quickly' as an expected score outcome

R3.strength: Honest framing: names report-backed INP suspects but labels them as guesses until measured, and ranks real-user TTFB as the second issue.
R3.mistake: No owner assigned to most fixes (only hosting), and it promises SEO/accessibility will reach the 90s.

R4.strength: Every card has plain meaning, owner (dev, content, marketing ops, host), effort and a concrete acceptance check; careful not to invent the theme name.
R4.mistake: Treats the 597 KiB Font Awesome JS only as a caching problem ('if unsure, keep the file and cache it') rather than an INP suspect, and suggests fixing the AddThis load instead of removing the dead script.

penalties.why: Gives the theme path as 'wp-content/themes/betabound'; the report only shows a truncated 'wp-content/themes/betab' path

R5.strength: Most complete field-vs-lab table and INP suspect list (viewport, Font Awesome JS with the DOM path evidence, Modernizr, Joyride, AddThis, Disqus, GTM), with WordPress-specific enqueue/defer fixes, an INP logger, and an explicit 'I have not measured anything'.
R5.mistake: Fills in the truncated theme folder name as 'betabound' and repeats it in both agent prompts as if confirmed.

R6.strength: Correct verdict and lab-vs-field explanation, every INP suspect tied to its audit evidence, WordPress-aware fixes with a 'Done when' check, and the right owners (marketing ops for AddThis, Disqus and GTM).
R6.mistake: Makes the viewport tag fix #1 and says it 'alone could explain most of your INP' (plus a '15 minutes' estimate) when the report gives no detail on that audit; it is labeled a hypothesis, but it is overweighted.
